title: architectureRules
responsibility: Checks directional import boundaries and requires named types to be separate from runtime implementations.

inputs.name: auditTypePlacement.file
inputs.description: The file to inspect: `contents` is parsed with the TypeScript parser (script kind from `relativePath`), but when `extension` is exactly '.svelte' only the joined `<script>` blocks are parsed. `relativePath` is also the path reported in findings and decides the '.d.ts' and '.types.ts' cases; only `relativePath`, `extension` and `contents` are read, so `absolutePath`, `lines`, `structuralLines`, `limits` and `size` have no effect.

examples.contents: {label}

inputs.name: auditArchitecture.path
inputs.description: Repository-relative path of the importing file, using forward slashes such as 'src/core/files.ts'; only paths starting with 'src/core/', 'src/templates/' or 'src/commands/' are checked, relative specifiers are resolved from its folder, and every finding repeats this value as its `path`. Other paths produce no findings.

inputs.name: auditArchitecture.lines
inputs.description: The importing file's source lines in order, where the element at index i is reported as line i + 1; only the first quoted `from` specifier on each line is checked, so side-effect `import`, `require()` and `import()` specifiers are never inspected. The TypeScript adapter passes `AuditFile.structuralLines`, which replaces template-literal text with spaces, so a `from` clause inside a backtick string is not seen.

outputs.name: auditArchitecture
outputs.description: Findings in line order, at most one per line, for core modules importing templates, workflows or commands, template modules importing workflows or commands, and command modules importing templates, core/files or core/fields; an empty array means no finding. Matching uses those folder names anywhere in the resolved import path, and the core and template rules also need a path segment after the folder, so a bare '../templates' specifier is not reported by them.

examples.message: Core modules cannot import templates, workflows, or commands. Import starts near line 1.
Command modules should delegate instead of importing templates or file-generation helpers. Import starts near line 1.
Template modules cannot import workflows or commands. Import starts near line 1.

outputs.name: auditTypePlacement
outputs.description: Empty for '.d.ts' files and for files with no top-level runtime statement (class, function, variable, enum, expression or export assignment; statements with a `declare` modifier do not count). A '.types.ts' file with runtime code gets one file-level finding, and any other file with runtime code gets one finding per interface or type alias at any depth.

examples.message: Move ReportOptions to a sibling .types.ts file and import its type.
Move Props to a sibling .types.ts file and import its type.
Keep runtime implementations outside type files; retain type-only declarations and compatibility re-exports here.
